newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek PM calls on farmers to lift blockades.
newsitem.headline: Greek PM calls on farmers to lift blockades.

text.p: Greek Prime Minister Costas Simitis appealed on Thursday to farmers to end their crippling eight-day blockade of national road and rail links, saying it was posing a serious threat to the economy.

"I appeal to everyone to understand how critical the situation is and to those who have taken over the national road network to free it," he said in his first public statements since the crisis began last Thursday.
The farmers, backing their demands with an army of some 10,000 tractors, have taken over more than 40 main junctions around the country. They have halted almost all commercial road and rail traffic.
Simitis said the government had nothing more to give and must pursue its economic policies without deviations to meet its European Union convergence targets.
"The government cannot agree to measures that will overturn its economic policy," said Simitis, who is facing his first major crisis since winning national elections in September.
